title: Um telefonema
en: A delivery driver can't find the house.

paragraphs.pt: O telemóvel toca. É um estafeta com uma encomenda. — Estou? — Boa tarde. Fala o estafeta. Tenho aqui uma encomenda para si. Está em casa?
paragraphs.en: The phone rings. It's a delivery driver with a parcel. “Hello?” “Good afternoon. This is the delivery driver. I have a parcel for you here. Are you at home?”

paragraphs.pt: — Estou, sim. Não encontra a casa? — Não. Estou na rua principal, ao pé da farmácia. — A minha casa é a terceira à direita, com a porta azul.
paragraphs.en: “Yes, I am. Can't you find the house?” “No. I'm on the main street, next to the pharmacy.” “My house is the third one on the right, with the blue door.”

paragraphs.pt: — Ah, já vejo! Chego daqui a dois minutos. — Obrigado. Espero lá fora. Dois minutos depois, a encomenda está na mão. Fácil!
paragraphs.en: “Ah, I can see it now! I'll be there in two minutes.” “Thanks. I'll wait outside.” Two minutes later, the parcel is in your hand. Easy!

options: On the main street, next to the pharmacy
The third on the right, with the blue door
The one with the red door
The one next to the café

questions.q: What does “Estou?” mean when you answer the phone?

glossary.daqui: from here (daqui a dois minutos = in two minutes)
glossary.estou: I am (estar); Estou? = Hello? on the phone
glossary.fala: speaks (falar); Fala o … = This is … on the phone

notes.en: Hello? This is how you answer the phone in Portugal.
This is the delivery driver (how callers say who they are).
for you. The polite form; in Portugal more natural than para você.
